the transcriptional regulation of the CDKNIA gene by PLZF-RARA, a transcriptional repressors of p21 and p53 genes, and its role in APL-type leukemia.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PLZF-RAR complex is a transcriptional co-repressor complex that represses the transcription of p21 and p53 genes by binding to their promoters, thereby increasing cell proliferation and contributing to APL-type leukemogenesis.

PLZF-RARA represses transcriptional activation of the CDKN 1A promoter by binding to Sp1, RARα and p53 binding elements, and by recruiting the histone de-acetylase and DNA methylase corepressors, and thereby represses p21 expression, which in turn leads to the promotion of cell proliferation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the oncogene transcriptional regulator PLZF-RAR represses transcription by interacting with the histone deactylase corepressor complex, MBD3-NURD complex, and ubiquitin ligase, and thereby represses the expression of CDKN1a, TP53, and RARA, and promotes cell proliferation in APL-type leukemia.

PLZF-R ARα represses the CDKN1 A gene by interacting with the transcription factors p53, R ARα, and Sp 1 and the histone-modifying and DNA methylation enzymes, leading to cell cycle deregulation and leukemogenesis.
PLZF-RAPα represses the expression of p21 and TP53, and thereby promotes cell proliferation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

PLZF-R ARα represses the expression of CDKN1 A and TP53, which are key regulators of the cell cycle, and that PLZF-R RARα promotes cell cycle progression by inhibiting the expression of these cell cycle regulators.
PLZF-RAPα represses p21 expression, and this repression contributes to the leukemic phenotype.
